issues.description: The template's Stock class declares findStockIngredient(String, boolean) while the problem statement UML and the solution expect findStockIngredient(String). Additionally, the template's add(String) and take(String) methods call findStockIngredient(ingredient) with a single String argument, which does not match the two-parameter declaration. This inconsistency will cause compilation errors and confuses students about the required method signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template Stock.findStockIngredient declaration to findStockIngredient(String name) (single parameter) to match the UML in the problem statement and the solution. Ensure the add(String) and take(String) methods call this single-parameter method. If case-sensitive matching is desired, implement it inside the single-parameter method or add an overloaded helper without changing the expected signature.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify Stock.findStockIngredient(String): StockIngredient (single-argument). The template Stock.java exposes findStockIngredient(String, boolean) (two-argument) while the solution implements findStockIngredient(String) (single-argument). This signature mismatch can confuse students mapping the UML/requirements to the starter code and tests because the expected single-argument method is absent in the template.
issues.suggestedFix: Add or restore the single-argument method public StockIngredient findStockIngredient(String name) in the template Stock class (it may delegate to the existing two-argument variant) so the template matches the UML/problem statement and the solution. Ensure the behavior (case sensitivity) matches the specification used in tests.
